texts.preamble: Kadagala Jagadish, vs The State Of A.P. on 24 March, 2022 Author: D.Ramesh Bench: D. Ramesh The Hon'Ble Sri Justice D. Ramesh Criminal Petition No.2054 Of 2022 Order:
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that this is a covered matter in view of the earlier common order passed by this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, whereby this Court has [LEAKAGE_MASK] several F.I.Rs registered for the similar offences based on identical facts. Therefore, he would submit that the petitioner is similarly placed and therefore entitled for quash of the F.I.R registered against him. 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch it was held that the police would not have jurisdiction to initiate or investigate any offences punishable under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and that transport or storage of tobacco and tobacco products would not constitute an offence punishable under Sections 270 to 273 of IPC. 5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor fairly concedes that this is a covered matter in view of the aforesaid common order passed by this Court and thereby prayed to pass appropriate orders accordingly in this Criminal Petition also.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that this is a covered matter in view of the earlier common order passed by this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, whereby this Court has [LEAKAGE_MASK] several F.I.Rs registered for the similar offences based on identical facts. Therefore, he would submit that the petitioner is similarly placed and therefore entitled for quash of the F.I.R registered against him. 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch it was held that the police would not have jurisdiction to initiate or investigate any offences punishable under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and that transport or storage of tobacco and tobacco products would not constitute an offence punishable under Sections 270 to 273 of IPC.
texts.respondent_arguments: 5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor fairly concedes that this is a covered matter in view of the aforesaid common order passed by this Court and thereby prayed to pass appropriate orders accordingly in this Criminal Petition also.
